title: The Lens
idiom: hand-coloured 19th-century steel engraving: a lens with no handle and no hand on a grey river valley, and only what is under the glass is in colour
hero_prompt: Hand-coloured 19th-century steel engraving, hand-made on paper, flat and graphic with visible engraved line and cross-hatching, not a photograph, not a 3D render, no depth-of-field, wide panoramic composition: a quiet river valley seen from above, rolling hills, a winding river, a small stone bridge and a few trees, all printed in plain grey-black ink on cream paper with no colour at all. Lying flat on the valley, a little left of centre, is one large round glass lens with a thin dark rim and no handle, nothing holding it, no hands, no people. Everything seen through the glass is hand-coloured in bold saturated washes of vermilion, ochre and cobalt, and the scene inside the circle is gently transformed rather than magnified: the river inside the glass curls into a bright ribbon, the hills swell into warm folds, while outside the rim the same river and hills continue in plain grey line. A clear seam where the coloured circle meets the grey engraving.
icon_prompt: Not rendered: cut from the hero. A square around the hero's lens (box 53,36–517,500 of the 1280x544 hero, after its 32px bottom trim), scaled to 1024x1024. Three FLUX icons were rejected first: a printmaker's signature on a life-buoy ring, bars that never crossed the rim, and an emblem that read as letters.
